expectations.text: Output contains 'Problem Statement' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Problem Statement' section. The document opens with '## 1. Overview' (line 3); there is no business/user-problem or success-criteria section anywhere.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Scope' section
expectations.evidence: No section titled 'Scope'. The Overview (lines 5-8) discusses what the area covers in prose but there is no In scope / Out of scope structure.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Capabilities' section

expectations.text: Output contains 'Dependency Map' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Dependency Map' section or any inter-capability dependency table. Closest is a 'Subscription State Model' (line 272), which is a status state machine, not a capability dependency map.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Open Questions' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Open Questions' section. Unresolved decisions are not surfaced as questions; the doc presents 'Edge cases' lists instead.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Research Suggestions' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Research Suggestions' section and no mention of further investigation to delegate.

expectations.text: Output contains 'Next Steps' section
expectations.evidence: No 'Next Steps' section. The doc ends with a 'Build vs Buy Note' (line 289) and a 'Capability Checklist' (line 295).

expectations.text: Depth level is marked as 'standard'
expectations.evidence: No depth marker anywhere. There is no 'Depth: standard' header line; title is just '# Subscription Management — Capability Breakdown' (line 1).

expectations.text: Covers 4-8 capabilities (standard depth)
expectations.evidence: The baseline enumerates ~12 capability domains (2.1-2.12, lines 31-251) plus cross-cutting concerns — well beyond the 4-8 standard-depth range. Not constrained to standard depth.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Trigger field
expectations.evidence: No 'Trigger' field on any capability. Capabilities are presented as tables of name/description, not the structured Trigger/Inputs/Logic flow format.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Inputs field
expectations.evidence: No 'Inputs' field exists for any capability.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Logic flow field
expectations.evidence: No 'Logic flow' field. Behavior is described in prose/table descriptions, not numbered logic flows.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Outputs field
expectations.evidence: No 'Outputs' field for any capability.

expectations.text: Each capability has an Edge cases field
expectations.evidence: Most domains include an '**Edge cases:**' line (e.g. line 46, 64, 82, 113, 130, 148, 168, 188, 206). Edge cases are present, though the other structured fields are not.

expectations.text: Each capability has a Connects to field
expectations.evidence: No 'Connects to' field; capabilities are not cross-referenced via dependency relationships or IDs.

expectations.text: Business problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: No Problem Statement section. The Overview implies business value ('the full lifecycle of a paid customer relationship', line 5) but never states a structured business problem.

expectations.text: User problem is stated in Problem Statement
expectations.evidence: No Problem Statement and no explicit user-problem statement.

expectations.text: Success criteria are measurable
expectations.evidence: No success criteria are defined anywhere. The doc lists metrics to track (MRR/ARR, churn, line 246) but states no measurable success targets for the feature.

expectations.text: Logic flows describe WHAT not HOW (no tech stack, no code, no architecture)
expectations.evidence: No logic flows exist, and the baseline repeatedly names tech stack / architecture: 'Stripe, Braintree, Adyen' (line 14), 'Stripe Billing, Chargebee, Recurly, Paddle' (line 291), '3-D Secure / SCA ... PSD2' (line 143), 'Use integer minor units ... never float' (line 262). This is HOW/implementation detail, contrary to the WHAT-not-HOW guideline.

expectations.evidence: Section '## 2.2 Signup & Subscription Creation' (line 50) with plan selection, checkout, first charge, activation.

expectations.evidence: '## 2.3 Billing Cycle & Recurring Charges' (line 68) and '## 2.8 Invoicing' (line 172).

expectations.evidence: '## 2.4 Plan Changes — Upgrade / Downgrade / Cancel' (line 86) and a dedicated '## 2.5 Proration' (line 117).

expectations.evidence: No CAP-NN identifiers anywhere; capabilities use section numbers (2.1-2.12) and there is no dependency map.

expectations.text: Research Suggestions reference the researcher skill
expectations.evidence: No Research Suggestions section and no reference to the researcher skill.

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to save/persist the output — suggests librarian skill instead
expectations.evidence: No mention of the librarian skill or any persistence guidance. (It did not erroneously save either, but it also does not suggest the librarian skill as the assertion requires.)

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to conduct its own research — flags topics for researcher skill
expectations.evidence: No researcher delegation. Instead the baseline asserts external facts on its own (e.g. 'ASC 606' rev-rec, line 246; SCA/PSD2 specifics, line 143) rather than flagging them for research.

expectations.text: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
expectations.evidence: No Existing Knowledge section and no librarian skill check; the doc starts directly with an Overview.

expectations.text: Flags at least 2 distinct research topics (e.g., dunning strategies, tax compliance)
expectations.evidence: No research topics are flagged for follow-up; the baseline answers such areas inline rather than identifying them as open research.

expectations.text: Edge cases cover payment method expiration scenarios
expectations.evidence: Section 2.7 edge cases: 'card expires between renewals' (line 168) and 'Card updater — Use account-updater services to refresh expiring/replaced cards' (line 165).

expectations.text: Edge cases cover proration edge cases (mid-cycle changes)
expectations.evidence: Section 2.5 Proration edge cases (line 130): 'proration combined with discounts/coupons; proration ... when the period anchor also changes; negative invoice'; Section 2.4 (line 113): 'changing plan and interval at the same time; multiple changes within one period'.

expectations.text: Connects to shows clear dependency relationships between capabilities
expectations.evidence: No 'Connects to' fields and no explicit dependency relationships between capabilities. Cross-cutting concerns are listed (section 3) but capabilities are not wired to one another.

claims.claim: The baseline produced a thorough, knowledgeable subscription-billing capability survey
claims.evidence: Content is broad and accurate (12 domains, cross-cutting concerns, state model). However it is a domain survey, not the solution-architect prescribed breakdown — it lacks the required structure entirely.

claims.claim: The baseline names specific implementation technologies
claims.evidence: Stripe/Braintree/Adyen (line 14), Stripe Billing/Chargebee/Recurly/Paddle (line 291), 3-D Secure/SCA/PSD2 (line 143) — confirming HOW-level detail the prescribed format forbids.

claims.claim: The baseline delegated research/persistence to other skills
claims.evidence: No references to researcher or librarian skills exist; the baseline neither delegated research nor suggested persistence.

suggestions.assertion: Covers payment failure handling as a capability
suggestions.reason: Domain-coverage assertions (signup, billing, proration, cancel, payment-failure, expiration/proration edge cases) all pass even for a baseline that ignores the prescribed format entirely — any competent LLM survey covers these subscription topics. These assertions are not discriminating between with-skill and baseline; the structural/format/delegation assertions are what actually separate them.

The genuine signal in this eval is structural conformance (named sections, CAP-NN IDs, per-capability fields), depth marking, WHAT-not-HOW discipline, and researcher/librarian delegation — all of which the baseline fails. These are well-covered, so the eval correctly distinguishes the skill. Consider de-weighting or consolidating the 6 generic topic-coverage assertions so the pass rate reflects skill-specific behavior rather than baseline domain knowledge.

eval_feedback.overall: Baseline passes only generic topic-coverage assertions (11/32) and fails every structure, format, depth, WHAT-not-HOW, and delegation assertion — exactly the prescribed behaviors the skill adds. The eval discriminates well between skill and no-skill.
